implementation_summary: Added signal and timeoutMs to AICompletionOptions. Added AUDIT_AI_STAGES (satisfies readonly AIStage[]), AuditAiStage, AuditAiModels, AuditAiModelsReply, AuditAiModelsUpdate, AuditAiModelsErrors, AuditAiModelsCheck, AUDIT_AI_MODEL_ID_MAX=200, isAuditAiStage, validateAuditAiModelsUpdate (ok/errors shape like validateAuditStartBody; refuses unknown stages, empty or non-string ids, ids over 200 chars, C0/DEL/C1 control characters; null resets a stage; a __proto__ key is stored as a plain field) and AUDIT_AI_API (GET/PUT /api/audit-ai/models, access owner, satisfies AuditEndpoint via a type-only import from ./website-audit.js). No Node built-in imports.
tests_proposed: Runner integration test: PUT /api/audit-ai/models refuses Helpers and requests without the access key, and returns validator errors as a 400.
risks: AUDIT_AI_API is separate from AUDIT_API, so the typed AuditApi route map in website-audit.ts does not cover these routes; the runner must register them and enforce owner access when it reads or writes the settings.
AI Providers do not use signal/timeoutMs yet; until they do, RISK-005 is not mitigated.
The validator has no cap on the number of keys; it relies on the runner's request-size limit.
handoff: Import from @qa/types (or @qa/types/src/ai.js in the wizard; ai.ts is not re-exported from browser.ts). Runner: serve AUDIT_AI_API.getModels/putModels as owner only, validate PUT bodies with validateAuditAiModelsUpdate (on failure return 400 with errors per field; on success a null value resets that stage to its default), and build the reply's effective map with modelForStage(stage, models, defaults). Providers: pass options.signal and options.timeoutMs to fetch, combining them, for example with AbortSignal.any plus AbortSignal.timeout.
